newsitem.title: UK: Lockheed confirms Russia Intersputnik tie-up.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed confirms Russia Intersputnik tie-up.

text.p: Lockheed Martin International, part of U.S military and aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp confirmed on Monday that it was establishing a joint venture -- to be headquartered in London -- with Russia's Intersputnik International Organsation of Space Communication to provide worldwide communication services via satellite.
Initially, LMI will provide communications to customers in eastern Europe, South Asia, Africa and the Commonwealth of Independent States.
Officials said broadcast and telecommunications services would expand to include direct-to-home video and audio and mobile services to customers worldwide.
"We are extremely pleased to have Intersputnik as partners in such an exciting venture," said Mel Brashears, president and chief operating officer of Lockheed's space and strategic missile sector.
"The combination of our two organisations results in a new and highly competiive global satellite services supplier," he said.
Lockheed declined to comment on when the venture would be profitable or how much the company was investing because of a highly competitive nature of the satellite telecomunications business.

Gennady Kudryavstev, director-general of Intersputnik, which was established over 25 years ago during the Cold War days and has 22 member countries, said the new company would provide cutting edge solutions to customers' communications needs.
"We will pursue excellence and growth through co-operation, continuous improvement and innovation," he said.

Lockheed Martins's pace and strategic missile sector designs, manufactures and supports a variety of advanced technology systems for domestic and international military, classified, civil and commercial markets.
